messages:
maria: Kicking off edge-onramp validation for sea4. Following the runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/edge-onramp. Provisioning + smoke tests started.

infra-bot: Provision job complete: 48x A100 nodes provisioned, subnets/route tables applied, LB attached. Logs: /ops/provision/2065502468

kevin: Quick sync — any network restrictions from the provider (egress caps, peering limits)? Also need a list of candidate canary models.

sophia: Noted intermittent 10% packet loss between AZ-b and AZ-c during the initial pod churn. Looks like MTU mismatch on one of the transit gateways.

kevin: Can someone run iperf across two problematic nodes? If MTU then we should see fragmentation or dropped frames.

david: Running quick iperf now from node-03 -> node-12:
```
$ iperf3 -c 10.12.3.12 -t 10
Connecting to host 10.12.3.12, port 5201
[  5] local 10.12.3.3 port 52044 connected to 10.12.3.12 port 5201
[ ID] Interval           Transfer     Bandwidth
[  5]   0.00-10.00  sec  8.24 GBytes  7.07 Gbits/sec  sender
[  5]   0.00-10.00  sec  8.24 GBytes  7.06 Gbits/sec  receiver
```

sophia: iperf shows good throughput on those two nodes — the loss is more noticeable at the kube-proxy level during rolling updates. MTU still suspicious. I'll open a ticket with network to check transit GW.

kevin: Also spotted a driver mismatch on node-07, nvidia-smi shows 530.30 vs 525.x expected. That can cause inconsistent GPU behaviour during model compile.

maria: Thanks — action items so far:
- @sophia raise network transit GW MTU ticket (blocked: yes)
- @david replace node-07 into maintenance, reimage with driver 525.x
- infra team: hold canary launch until both fixed

kevin: For readiness gates — propose we require all of: 
- network loss < 0.5% across AZs under churn
- p95 generation latency <= 120ms for 512-token test
- sustained throughput >= 180 qps on the dedicated pool
- model compile success 100% across nodes

sophia: Ran a quick model warmup (2 small GPT models) — cold-start p95 spikes to ~900ms, after warmup p95 ~95ms. KV cache warmup policy needs to be in the runbook (prefetch prefixes).

maria: Posting the benchmark fragment (small synthetic):
```
model: redwood-mini-1
batch 1: p50 42ms p95 92ms
batch 4: p50 75ms p95 115ms
throughput (steady): 190 qps
```

kevin: Nice baseline. But note GPU util is uneven across fleet (node skew). Need autoscaler policy tweak: prefer binpack by GPU-util then fill.

infra-bot: Automated checklist results:
- Provisioning: ✅ 48 nodes live
- LB healthchecks: ✅ 100% healthy
- Kernel/driver consistency: ❌ node-07 mismatch
- Network packet-loss (AZs): ⚠️ intermittent (10% windows)
- Smoke inference p95 (512 tokens): ⚠️ 95ms warm, 900ms cold spikes
- Billing estimate: ✅ ~$6.4/hr/node (pre-reserved)

maria: Given infra-bot, recommendation = HOLD canary. Do not route prod or PLG traffic. We can proceed with an isolated internal canary test once node-07 is reprovisioned and network MTU fixed.

david: I'll reprovision node-07 now and run driver/firmware validation; ETA 25m.

sophia: I've created NET-3421 for transit GW MTU with network team; they assigned an on-call. ETA 2h for full verification, might be quicker.

kevin: Cost note — if we keep 48 nodes reserved, go/no-go affects commit discussion with finance. If we move to burst mode (dedicated->shared) short term, unit-cost goes up ~18%. I'll ping finance if timeline slips past EOD.

maria: Plan: repossess node-07 + driver, monitor packet loss, rerun smoke and model compile, then schedule a 30m readiness review with PMs. Owners: david (node reprovision), sophia (net ticket), kevin (autoscaler + cost), maria (readiness review).

infra-bot: @maria created checklist run: /ops/checks/2065502468/results (status: HOLD)

maria: Ok team — thanks. I'll update the runbook with the MTU and driver troubleshooting steps and add a pre-canary KV cache warmup step. Will post when ready for the handoff review. :thumbsup:
